turns.user: Buildability check: 500 mm wall, 2 m long, 25 mm nozzle, 40 mm/s. Rheometer gives a static yield stress of 0.004 MPa and a structuration rate of 60 Pa per minute.
turns.text:
I’ll run the buildability calculation with the wall and rheometer inputs, then report the governing failure mode and any required assumptions.
**Verdict: non-printable as a free-standing, single-filament wall.** The physical check predicts buckling at layer 11, about 138 mm high, before the 500 mm target. Plastic collapse is also a concern: with the safety factor applied, its limit is about 23 of the required 40 layers. The empirical collapse probability is 56%, but the physical failure checks govern this verdict.

The calculator assumed 12.5 mm layers, a 29.61 mm wall width, 2,100 kg/m³ fresh density, and an elastic modulus equal to 25 times the measured static yield stress. At 40 mm/s, each 2 m layer takes 50 s, with no dwell time. Your rheometer inputs were converted to 4,000 Pa and 1 Pa/s.

For **plastic stability**, the calculator gives a minimum cycle time of 123 s, or requires about 6,920 Pa initial static yield stress or 2.46 Pa/s structuration at the current 50 s cycle. Slowing the cycle alone does not resolve the predicted buckling. A thicker or braced wall needs a new check; measured fresh density and elastic modulus would also improve it. Open time was not supplied, so its limit remains unverified.

A similar published straight-wall run reached 450 mm with 3,642 Pa static yield stress and 1.63 Pa/s structuration, but it used a 30 mm nozzle and does not establish that this wall will succeed. Verify the final geometry and mix with a trial print.
